source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Measured Moves Based on Gaps and Trading Ranges

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: BullTrendBar
candidates.quote: the breakout bar is a relatively large bull trend bar and the low of the next bar is above the breakout point
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar is a bull trend bar (closed up, body is most of the range).
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: single-bar OHLC arithmetic

notes: Brooks gives no number; 0.6 is a reading of a body that dominates the bar.

candidates.name: LargeTrendBar
candidates.quote: the breakout bar is a relatively large bull trend bar
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bull trend bar whose range is at least K times the N-bar ATR.
candidates.pseudocode: R08-01 && (high[0] - low[0]) >= rangeMultiple * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: needs an ATR window

notes: 'Relatively large' is read as a multiple of ATR.

candidates.name: DojiBar
candidates.quote: wait for the first small bull trend bar, bear trend bar, or doji bar. Its low is then the top of the gap.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar has a tiny body relative to its range.
candidates.pseudocode: abs(close[0] - open[0]) <= dojiFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic

candidates.name: GapUpBar
candidates.quote: Gaps are common on daily charts where the low of one bar is above the high of the prior bar
candidates.description: The current bar gapped above the prior bar (true gap). Used as a continuation entry and as the trigger that defines a measuring gap.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (gap is a chart feature; trade with the gap direction)

complexity.reason: two-bar price comparison

notes: Brooks: 'if there is conviction about the direction of the market, the middle of the gap often becomes the middle of the trend.'

candidates.name: GapMidpointMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: Traders measured from the bar 1 bottom of the rally to the middle of the gap and then projected that same number of points upward.
candidates.description: After a gap-up bar g, gapMid = (low[g] + high[g+1]) / 2; legStart = lowest low over legLookback bars ending at g; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart). Exit the long when the high reaches the target within a tolerance.
candidates.pseudocode: gapMid = (low[g] + high[g+1]) / 2; legStart = lowest(low, legLookback)[g]; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: target persists from a detected gap bar and needs the start of the leg that contains it

notes: Emini traders regard a target as tested only within one tick (p76); toleranceTicks encodes that.
Brooks: look at the nearest target first (p77).

candidates.name: BreakoutAboveSwingHigh
candidates.quote: if the market breaks out above a swing high and the breakout bar is a relatively large bull trend bar
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the bar closes above the highest high of the prior N bars (breakout point = that highest high).
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutPoint = highest(high, lookback)[1]; close[0] > breakoutPoint
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the swing high

complexity.reason: highest-high window

candidates.name: BreakoutGapHolds
candidates.quote: the low of the next bar is above the breakout point, then there is a gap between that low and the breakout point and that often becomes a measuring gap
candidates.description: The prior bar was a large-trend-bar breakout above the N-bar high and this bar's low stayed above the breakout point: an intraday measuring gap has formed; enter/hold long.
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutPoint = highest(high, lookback)[2]; close[1] > breakoutPoint && LargeTrendBar[1] && low[0] > breakoutPoint
candidates.book_order_type: with-trend swing; the gap is a hold signal rather than an order

complexity.reason: cross-bar state: breakout bar identity and its breakout point

candidates.name: GapTopFromFirstNonTrendBar
candidates.quote: If the bar after the breakout is also a large bull trend bar, then wait for the first small bull trend bar, bear trend bar, or doji bar. Its low is then the top of the gap.
candidates.description: Primitive for the measuring-gap top: after the breakout bar, scan forward; the first bar that is not a large bull trend bar (small bull, bear body, or doji) defines gapTop = its low.
candidates.pseudocode: isNonTrend = !LargeTrendBar[0] || close[0] < open[0] || DojiBar[0]; first such bar after breakout: gapTop = low[0]

complexity.reason: forward scan state after a breakout event

candidates.name: MeasuringGapTarget
candidates.quote: line B is the midpoint of the thin area in between the breakout (the high of bar 2) and the low of the first pullback (the low of bar 5). The measured move was hit to the exact tick
candidates.description: gapMid = (breakoutPoint + gapTop) / 2 where gapTop = low of the first pullback/pause bar within pullbackWindowBars of the breakout; legStart = lowest low over legLookback bars before the breakout; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart). Exit long when high reaches target.
candidates.pseudocode: gapMid = (breakoutPoint + gapTop) / 2; legStart = lowest(low, legLookback)[b]; target = gapMid + (gapMid - legStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the projection; swing part of the position until reached

complexity.reason: measured-move target from breakout point, first-pullback low and leg start

notes: If the pullback low falls inside the gap within a few bars the gap shrinks but its midpoint is still used (p76).
Brooks: 'Once there is a breakout flag, it is wise to swing part of your with-trend trade until the measured move is reached.' (p78)

candidates.name: BreakoutBarMidpointTarget
candidates.quote: the market will often just use the middle of the breakout bar as the middle of the gap. In this case, the measured move is based on the start of the rally to the middle of the breakout bar.
candidates.description: Fallback measured move when the breakout point or pullback is unclear: mid = (high[b] + low[b]) / 2 of the breakout bar; target = mid + (mid - legStart).
candidates.pseudocode: mid = (high[b] + low[b]) / 2; legStart = lowest(low, legLookback)[b]; target = mid + (mid - legStart); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: target persists from an identified breakout bar; only a lowest-low window otherwise

notes: Ch12 restates it: every trend bar is a breakout bar and a gap bar (p77).

candidates.name: NegativeGapUnreliableTarget
candidates.quote: Since the difference between the breakout pullback and the breakout point is then a negative number, I call this a negative gap. Measured move projections are less reliable when they are based on a negative gap.
candidates.description: Filter: only rely on a measuring-gap target (or only swing for it) when the pullback low after the breakout stayed above the breakout point (positive gap).
candidates.pseudocode: pullbackLow = lowest(low, pullbackWindowBars) after breakout bar b; pullbackLow - breakoutPoint > 0

complexity.reason: needs the breakout bar and a window after it

candidates.name: NegativeGapRangeHeightTarget
candidates.quote: more commonly the end of the measured move will be equal to the top of the breakout point, here the bar 2 high, minus the bottom of the initial trading range, here the bar 1 low.
candidates.description: When the gap is negative, target = breakoutPoint + (breakoutPoint - rangeBottom), rangeBottom = lowest low of the trading range before the breakout.
candidates.pseudocode: rangeBottom = lowest(low, rangeLookback)[b]; target = breakoutPoint + (breakoutPoint - rangeBottom); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: breakout bar state plus a lowest-low window

notes: Identical arithmetic to R08-13; differs only in when Brooks reaches for it.

candidates.name: TradingRangeHeightTarget
candidates.quote: Most traders use the height of the prior trading range for measuring, which is fine because the exact distance is only approximate no matter how you do it
candidates.description: After a breakout above an N-bar range, target = rangeHigh + (rangeHigh - rangeLow); exit long when the high reaches it.
candidates.pseudocode: rangeHigh = highest(high, rangeLookback)[b]; rangeLow = lowest(low, rangeLookback)[b]; target = rangeHigh + (rangeHigh - rangeLow); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: target frozen at the breakout bar; windows otherwise

notes: Could be made stateless: exit when high[0] >= 2 * highest(high, N)[k] - lowest(low, N)[k] for the bar k when the breakout happened.

candidates.name: CountertrendOnlyAtMeasuredMove
candidates.quote: The key is to trade only with the trend, but once the market is in the area of the measured move, you can begin to look for countertrend entries.
candidates.description: Filter for countertrend (short) entries in a bull leg: permit them only once the high has reached the measured-move target area.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] >= target - nearTargetAtr * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: depends on a measured-move target

notes: Brooks adds (p78): 'Just being in the area of a measured move is not enough reason for a countertrend entry. You need some earlier countertrend strength.' See R08-15.

candidates.name: CountertrendRequiresPriorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: the best countertrend trades only follow an earlier countertrend move that was strong enough to break the trend line.
candidates.description: Filter: a countertrend entry is allowed only if within the last N bars a countertrend move closed beyond the trend line drawn through the prior two swing lows (bull trend).
candidates.pseudocode: trendLine = line through last two swing lows; exists i in [0..lookback): close[i] < trendLine[i]

complexity.reason: needs pivot detection and trend-line projection

notes: Figure 8.4: strong bear trend with no trend line break, so stick to with-trend setups.

candidates.name: TwoLegsThenTwoLegCorrection
candidates.quote: Two legs often complete a move, and the move is usually followed by at least a protracted countertrend move that has at least two legs
candidates.description: After two with-trend legs reach the measured-move area, exit the with-trend swing (and expect a two-legged countertrend move that often tests the breakout point).
candidates.pseudocode: legCount >= legsToComplete && high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: take profits; swing part of a countertrend entry

complexity.reason: leg counting has no agreed mechanical definition

candidates.name: CountertrendTargetAtBreakoutPoint
candidates.quote: The countertrend move will often test all the way back to the breakout point.
candidates.description: For a countertrend short taken at a measured-move target (long side: a countertrend long taken at a downside target), the profit target is the earlier breakout point.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= breakoutPoint + toleranceTicks * tickSize  (long side of the mirror: high[0] >= breakoutPoint - toleranceTicks * tickSize)
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit at the breakout point

complexity.reason: needs the remembered breakout point of the prior leg

candidates.name: ThinAreaLowBarOverlap
candidates.quote: A thin area is a breakout area where there is very little overlap of the bars.
candidates.description: Primitive/continuation: over the last N bars each bar overlaps its prior bar by at most F of the prior bar's range (a thin, one-sided breakout leg).
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 0..spikeBars-1: (min(high[i], high[i+1]) - max(low[i], low[i+1])) <= overlapFraction * (high[i+1] - low[i+1])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (leg quality test; the thin area's midpoint is the measured-move midpoint)

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop of two-bar comparisons

notes: Direction-agnostic as written; pair with R08-01 for a bull thin area.

candidates.name: NoFadeAfterConsecutiveTrendBars
candidates.quote: the signal bar was the third consecutive strong bull trend bar. This was too much momentum to be a reliable short.
candidates.description: Filter blocking countertrend shorts when the signal bar is the Nth (or later) consecutive bull trend bar; long side: block countertrend longs after N consecutive bear trend bars.
candidates.pseudocode: consecutiveBearTrendBars(bodyFraction) < maxConsecutive  (blocks a countertrend long; mirror for shorts)

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop over recent bars

candidates.name: ClimacticConsecutiveTrendBarsExit
candidates.quote: Since bar 13 was the sixth consecutive bull trend bar, the momentum up was still strong. When this much strength occurs after a protracted bull trend, it sometimes represents a climactic exhaustion
candidates.description: Take (partial or full) profits on a long when the bar is the Nth consecutive bull trend bar after a protracted trend.
candidates.pseudocode: consecutiveBullTrendBars(bodyFraction) >= climaxBars && ctx.OpenPositionProfit() > 0

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop plus open profit

notes: Monthly AAPL example; Brooks says take profits but do not initiate shorts on that alone.

candidates.name: TwoBarReversal
candidates.quote: It might be in the process of forming a two-bar reversal, which could lead to a deeper correction that could have a couple of legs and last for 10 or more bars.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bear trend bar followed by a bull trend bar of comparable size that closes above the bear bar's midpoint (bull two-bar reversal).
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && R08-01[0] && close[0] > (high[1] + low[1]) / 2 && (high[0] - low[0]) >= sizeRatio * (high[1] - low[1])
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the second bar's high

complexity.reason: two-bar OHLC arithmetic

candidates.name: SpikeHeightMeasuredMove
candidates.quote: The five-bar spike down to bar 13 led to a measured move down, and the low of the day missed it by a tick.
candidates.description: After a spike of N consecutive bull trend bars ending at bar e and starting at bar s, target = high[e] + (high[e] - low[s]); exit long when the high reaches it.
candidates.pseudocode: spike = consecutiveBullTrendBars >= spikeBars; target = high[e] + (high[e] - low[s]); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: spike endpoints must persist after the spike ends

notes: Ch12 (p98) states the same as 'doubling the height of the spike'.

candidates.name: LateSessionMeasuredMoveUnlikely
candidates.quote: it was so late in the day that a measured move from its midpoint was unlikely to be reached.
candidates.description: Filter: do not initiate a measured-move swing when fewer than N bars remain in the session.
candidates.pseudocode: barsRemainingInSession(sessionEndTime) >= minBarsRemaining

complexity.reason: needs bar time and session end

candidates.name: TrendDayWithTrendOnly
candidates.quote: at that point the day was clearly a bear trend day and traders should only be shorting unless there was a clear and strong long scalp
candidates.description: Filter: on a trend day (session close-to-date far from session open, most closes on one side of the EMA), take only with-trend entries.
candidates.pseudocode: (close[0] - sessionOpen) >= trendDayAtr * atr(atrLookback) && fractionOfSessionBarsAboveEma >= minFraction  (bull trend day; allows longs only)

complexity.reason: 'trend day' needs a design decision; the pseudocode is one proxy

candidates.name: EmaGapBarAsCountertrendStrength
candidates.quote: since there had yet to be a sharp rally (like a gap bar above the exponential moving average), countertrend trades had to be scalps
candidates.description: Filter: allow a countertrend swing (long in a bear trend) only if within the last N bars a bar formed entirely above the EMA (a moving-average gap bar).
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [0..lookback): low[i] > ema(emaLength)[i]

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window scan

notes: Without it, countertrend trades are scalps only (or skipped).

candidates.name: LowerHighAfterMajorTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: the move to bar 9 broke a major trend line, setting up the bar 10 lower high test of the trend extreme (bar 8), and the subsequent bear trend that followed.
candidates.description: Long side (mirror of the book's short): after a countertrend rally broke the major bear trend line, the next test of the trend low forms a higher low with a bull reversal bar; enter long.
candidates.pseudocode: majorTrendLineBroken && low[0] > lowest(low, trendLookback)[1] && bullReversalBar[0]
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the lower-high signal bar (book); mirrored here

complexity.reason: major trend line detection plus swing test

candidates.name: DoubleBottomBullFlagBreakoutTarget
candidates.quote: This breakout above the double bottom bull flag projected up to line H.
candidates.description: After a breakout above a double-bottom bull flag, target = flagTop + (flagTop - flagBottom); exit long when the high reaches it.
candidates.pseudocode: target = flagHigh + (flagHigh - flagLow); high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: double-bottom flag recognition

notes: Chapter 12 develops the flag itself; the dedup pass should merge with R12 targets.

candidates.name: HorizontalWedgeFlagIsFinalFlag
candidates.quote: The small wedge bear flag around bar 4 was mostly horizontal and therefore a possible final bear flag
candidates.description: Filter/context: a three-push flag that is nearly horizontal (its highs and lows within a small ATR band) late in a trend flags a possible final flag; treat the next with-trend breakout with suspicion (scalp only).
candidates.pseudocode: threePushes && (highest(high, flagBars) - lowest(low, flagBars)) <= flatAtr * atr(atrLookback)

complexity.reason: three-push recognition

rejected.quote: On a Market Profile, these intraday measuring gaps where the market moves quickly are thin areas between two distributions
rejected.reason: volume-profile data the engine does not have; the bar-overlap proxy is kept as R08-18

rejected.quote: There were certainly news announcements that the television pundits used to explain all of the moves

chapter_summary: Short chapter on measured-move targets built from gaps (true gaps and intraday measuring gaps between a breakout point and the first pullback), from trading-range height, and from spike height. It produced a family of Exit targets (R08-05, 09, 10, 12, 13, 22, 27), the primitives they need (trend bar, large trend bar, doji, breakout above swing high, thin area), and context filters about when countertrend trades are permitted (measured-move area, prior trend line break, EMA gap bar, consecutive trend bars). Figures are mostly examples; the four-bar breakout-then-gap construction on p76 is the rule-like core.
